import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 674

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/674](https://www.erdosproblems.com/674)
- [Ko40] Ko, Chao, *Note on the Diophantine equation $x^xy^y=z^z$*. J. Chinese Math. Soc.
  (1940), 31-39.
-/

namespace Erdos674

/-- The set of integer solutions to $x^x y^y = z^z$ with $x, y, z > 1$. -/
def solutionSet : Set (ℕ × ℕ × ℕ) :=
  {(x, y, z) | 1 < x ∧ 1 < y ∧ 1 < z ∧ x ^ x * y ^ y = z ^ z}

/--
Are there any integer solutions to $x^xy^y=z^z$ with $x,y,z>1$?

Ko [Ko40] proved there are none if $(x,y)=1$, but there are in fact infinitely many solutions in
general - for example, $x=2^{12}3^6$, $y = 2^83^8$, and $z = 2^{11}3^7$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos674.lean"]
theorem erdos_674 : answer(True) ↔ solutionSet.Nonempty := by
  sorry

/--
There are in fact infinitely many integer solutions to $x^xy^y=z^z$ with $x,y,z>1$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/plby/lean-proofs/blob/main/src/v4.29.1/ErdosProblems/Erdos674.lean"]
theorem erdos_674.variants.infinite : solutionSet.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos674

findings.description: The module bibliography gives the page range for [Ko40] as “(1940), 31-39.” The cited paper appeared on pages 205–207. This is only a reference slip; the mathematical declarations are unaffected.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/bibs/Ko40 gives “J. Chinese Math. Soc. (1940), 205-207.” This is independently corroborated by reference [1] on p. 70 of Erdős, Some unconventional problems in number theory (https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1979-22.pdf), and reference [1] on p. 243 of Uchiyama, On the diophantine equation x^x y^y=z^z (https://www.mathnet.ru/eng/tm2337): volume 2 (1940), pp. 205–207.
findings.suggested_fix: Change the [Ko40] citation to “J. Chinese Math. Soc. 2 (1940), 205-207.”

reformulations.difference: The source speaks of integer solutions, whereas the definition uses triples of natural numbers.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: All three coordinates must exceed 1. Coordinatewise coercion ℕ → ℤ therefore bijects this solution set with the integer solution set, with inverse given by Int.toNat. Coercion preserves multiplication and powers, and the lower bounds ensure that converting the integer exponents to natural numbers loses nothing. In scratch.lean I proved the image equality and injectivity, then proved equivalences for both Nonempty and Infinite.

review.notes: All three declarations were checked. The existence question, its affirmative answer, and the infinitude variant match the source. Lean tests exclude every triple with a coordinate ≤ 1, find no solutions in the box 0–20, and independently verify the displayed solution (2985984, 1679616, 4478976). The cited infinitude proof was compiled separately, without its independent large-computation existence theorem; its axiom list is exactly [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]. The independent existence and equivalence proofs likewise contain no sorryAx. Both solved tags and formal-proof records are supported. Ko’s original 1940 article itself was not retrieved; its results and pagination were corroborated by the cited website and the Erdős/Uchiyama papers. The reviewed file remains unchanged.
